questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of school refusal?

options.text: Sudden onset associated with school transition

questions.explanation: . Educational underachievement is often a feature of truancy - not school refusal; this may be used to differentiate these two causes for school absence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following childhood psychiatric disorder has the highest heritability factor?
questions.explanation: . ADHD has the highest heritability among the listed conditions. Heritability of ADHD is estimated to be around 70 -80%. Heritability of school refusal is less than 40%. Conduct disorders show a heritability around 50%.

questions.question_text: When compared to children, which one of the following clinical features of depression is seen more commonly in adolescents?
questions.explanation: . Young children with depression show poor feeding, failure to thrive, tantrums, irritability, separation anxiety, hyperactivity, regressed behaviour such as enuresis, soiling, etc. Older children display somatisation (pain in the head, abdomen, chest), hypochondriacal ideas, school refusal, a drop in academic achievement at school, a decline in school work, sleep disturbance, antisocial behaviour. In adolescent low mood may not be fixed and pervasive and is more influenced by environment. Anhedonia and social withdrawal are powerful indicators of the presence of depression. Other features may include low self-esteem, biological symptoms, suicidal acts, behavioural problems, and substance abuse.

questions.question_text: In children with PANDAS which symptoms are least common?
questions.explanation: While OCD and tics are common, psychosis is extremely rare in PANDAS.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about Wechsler intelligence scale for children (WISC -R) are true except

options.text: It covers age range from 6 to 16 years
Commonly the tests are divided into verbal and performance categories yielding a verbal and performance IQ.
Object assembly and coding is a subtest to assess performance IQ
It is helpful for assessment of general intelligence in school age children
Twelve subtests are usually used, measuring different aspects of the child's ability

correct_answer.text: Twelve subtests are usually used, measuring different aspects of the child's ability

correct_answers.text: Twelve subtests are usually used, measuring different aspects of the child's ability

questions.explanation: . Wechsler intelligence scale for children (WISC -R) is helpful for the assessment of general intelligence in school age children. It covers age range from 6 to 16 years. Commonly the tests are divided into verbal and performance categories, yielding a verbal and performance IQ. Ten subtests are usually used, measuring different aspects of the child's ability. Each subtest has a mean score of 10 so that combining the 10 tests gives a full -scale IQ of 100 with a standard deviation of 15.

questions.question_text: About 90% of children are dry at night by the age of
questions.explanation: . Voluntary control does not begin until 15 -18 months. Most children are reasonably dry by day at 18 months. By 2 years 50% are dry at night, by 3 years 75% are dry at night and by 5 years 90% are dry at night.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a feature seen in truants rather than school refusers?
questions.explanation: Truancy is phenomenologically different from School Refusal. School Refusers are characterised by the presence of emotional rather than antisocial symptoms, with a familial tendency towards neurosis rather than antisocial behaviour, with parents being over -protective rather than inconsistent. The academic achievement in school refusers is usually satisfactory whereas truants have a poor track record. Small family size is associated with school refusal while larger families have more truants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about Tourette's disorder?

options.text: Females are more affected than males
Antipsychotics are the first line treatment
Mean age of onset is 12 years
Diagnosed by having both motor and vocal tics for 12 months
Diagnosed by having both motor and vocal tics for 6 months

correct_answer.text: Diagnosed by having both motor and vocal tics for 12 months

correct_answers.text: Diagnosed by having both motor and vocal tics for 12 months

questions.explanation: . Tourette's syndrome is characterized by multiple motor and one or more vocal tics, present for at least a year, causing distress and impaired function. The tics occur many times a day (usually in bouts) nearly every day or intermittently over more than 1 year, during which time there must not have been a tic free period of more than 3 consecutive months.

questions.question_text: Blockade of which of the following receptors can reduce vocal and motor tics seen in Tourette's syndrome?
questions.explanation: . Tics are reduced by D2 antagonism at basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: Genetic loading is a significant contributing factor to all of the following except
questions.explanation: . Though meta -analytic reviews of behavioral genetic studies of antisocial behaviour suggest that approximately 40% -50% of the variance can be explained by genetic influences (Rhee and Waldman, 2002; Miles and Carey, 1997), the influence of genetic inheritance is considered to be less prominent than the environment in terms of conduct disorder phenotype. Callous traits, in particular, show higher heritability than other traits of conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a true statement about bipolar disorder in children and adolescents?

options.text: Lamotrigine is used, if treatment resistant manic episodes are present
Manic children typically present with atypical or mixed features
The course is often episodic and of brief duration
60-70% of initial presentations are a manic episode

correct_answer.text: Manic children typically present with atypical or mixed features

correct_answers.text: Manic children typically present with atypical or mixed features

questions.explanation: . Those who develop bipolar disorder at a younger age, particularly in adolescence, may be more likely to have mixed bipolar disorder. Prevalence of bipolar disorder (BD) in youth may be as high as 1%. The most common comorbidities are ADHD (greater than 50%) and anxiety disorders. The rate of comorbid substance use increases in adolescence. Approximately 20% of youth with MDD will be diagnosed with bipolar disorder later in life. Equal gender distribution is characteristic (unlike MDD); however F:M ratio for rapid cycling BD is closer to 3:1.

questions.question_text: Which of the following risk factors is associated with autism?
questions.explanation: . The risk of autism was associated with breech presentation (risk ratio (RR) = 1.63), low Apgar score at 5 minutes (RR = 1.89), gestational age at birth <35 weeks (RR = 2.45), and parental psychiatric history (schizophrenia -like psychosis: RR = 3.44 and affective disorder: RR = 2.91). Analyses showed no statistically significant association between risk of autism and weight for gestational age, parity, number of antenatal visits, parental age, or socioeconomic status.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following treatments is most helpful for treating PTSD in children?
questions.explanation: . The results of a randomized controlled trial found that community -provided trauma -focused cognitive behavior therapy (TF -CBT) successfully improves posttraumatic stress disorder and anxiety in children exposed to specific trauma (e.g. intimate partner violence).

questions.question_text: The prevalence of ADHD in the UK is
questions.explanation: . The reported prevalence of ADHD in school age children worldwide varies from 1.7% to 17.8% depending on the criteria used. Most estimates lie between 5% and 10% when DSM -IV was used. US estimates have historically been higher than UK estimates, presumably due to the application of narrower diagnostic criteria by UK authors. Three studies of English populations have shown a prevalence rate of between 2% and 5%, depending on whether DSM or ICD -10 criteria were applied.

questions.question_text: The sex distribution is equal in which of the following conditions
questions.explanation: . The prevalence of separation anxiety disorder is slightly greater in females than in males. The prevalence of school refusal is approximately equal for males and females.

questions.question_text: In a 7-year-old child with uncomplicated Tourette's syndrome, the drug treatment of choice is
questions.explanation: . The most recent practice guidelines for Tourette's syndrome in children provide a three tiered pharmacological approach. The first tier is comprised of alpha 2 adrenergic agonists such as clonidine, the second tier comprised of drugs such as anticonvulsant topiramate used for many decades as off -label prescriptions, and the third -line comprised of D2 blocking agents such as haloperidol.

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients with autism has mental retardation?
questions.explanation: . The high rate of mental retardation among children with autistic disorder and the higher -than-expected rates of seizure disorders further support the biological basis for autistic disorder. Approximately 70 percent of children with autistic disorder have mental retardation. About one -third of these children have mild to moderate mental retardation, and close to half of these children are severely or profoundly mentally retarded.

questions.question_text: The ratio of prevalence of ADHD in males to females is
questions.explanation: . The estimated prevalence of ADHD is 4% to 12% in school -age children. ADHD is believed to be more common in males. Male -female ratios range from 9:1 to 6:1 in clinical samples but are about 4:1 in community -based population studies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a characteristic feature of PTSD in children?

options.text: Intrusive re-experiencing of a traumatic event

questions.explanation: . The diagnostic criteria for PTSD in DSM -IV was designed for adults, not children. Children have limited verbal skills and different ways of reacting to stress. This means that children may not fulfill the DSM -IV criteria, even though they clearly have a psychiatric disorder analogous to adult PTSD.

questions.question_text: A child is hyperactive and distractible in school and at home. Choose the risk factor associated with the development of this condition?
questions.explanation: . The diagnosis of this child is ADHD. 'Although genetic influences accounted for most of the variance in offspring ADHD, maternal smoking during pregnancy was still found to show a significant environmentally mediated association. Maternal smoking during pregnancy appears to show an association with offspring ADHD symptoms that is additional to the effects of genes and not attributable to shared rater effects, clinical referral biases, or variation with antisocial behaviour.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-old boy was interviewed to identify the presence of psychiatric disease. What scale could be used again at the age of 20?
questions.explanation: . The Clinical Interview Schedule - Revised is a fully structured diagnostic instrument that was developed from an existing instrument, the Clinical Interview Schedule (CIS), which was designed for the use of clinically experienced interviewers such as psychiatrists.

questions.question_text: You want to follow -up the progress in symptoms for a period of 4 years in patients diagnosed with depression at the age of 14. Which clinical instrument is most useful?

options.text: Child and adolescent functional assessment scale

correct_answer.text: Child and adolescent functional assessment scale

correct_answers.text: Child and adolescent functional assessment scale

questions.explanation: . The Child and Adolescent Functional Assessment Scale is a rating scale to assess the degree of impairment in functioning due to emotional, behavioural, or psychiatric problems.

questions.question_text: The blood abnormalities seen in Anorexia Nervosa include;
questions.explanation: . The blood abnormalities seen in anorexia include moderate normocytic normochromic anaemia, mild leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis and thrombocytopenia.

questions.question_text: What is the average age of onset of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: . The average age of onset is 25; it may be delayed in females and earlier in males.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about suicidal behaviour in adolescents is true?

options.text: Most adolescents who make suicide attempts actually have a psychiatric disorder
Suicide is the leading cause of death for adolescents
1% of adolescents who attempt suicide repeat within a year
Female suicides outnumber male suicides at all ages
Self-poisoning is the commonest form of parasuicide

correct_answer.text: Self-poisoning is the commonest form of parasuicide

correct_answers.text: Self-poisoning is the commonest form of parasuicide

questions.explanation: . Suicide is the third leading cause of death for adolescents, following accidents and homicides. Few adolescents who make suicide attempts actually have a psychiatric disorder and serious suicidal intent is generally low but if present, can be serious. Self-poisoning is the commonest form of parasuicide, the usual agents being analgesics and psychotropic agents.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of suicidal ideations in the past year for adolescent cohort in Britain is
questions.explanation: . Suicidal ideation (without deliberate self-harm) in the past year was reported by 15.0% of an adolescent cohort in UK (school pupils - self-report). This was more common in females (22%) than males (8.5%) (Odds ratio 3.1).

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric emergency seen in child and adolescent population is;
questions.explanation: . Suicidal behaviours are the most common emergency seen in this age group. Others are less common. Sexually inappropriate behaviour is rarely an emergency.

questions.question_text: Preschoolers and school -age children who stutter exhibit an increased incidence of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: . Stuttering is a condition in which the normal flow of speech is disrupted by involuntary speech motor events. Stuttering can include a variety of specific disruptions of fluency, including sound or syllable repetitions, sound prolongations, dysrhythmic phonation, and complete blocking or unusual pauses between sounds and syllables of words.

questions.question_text: The overall prevalence of psychiatric problems in adolescence is
questions.explanation: . Studies suggest that 20 percent of children and adolescents have mental health problems at some point, and one in ten have a clinically recognisable mental health disorder.

questions.question_text: A child with ADHD and congenital heart disease. What is the medication of choice?
questions.explanation: . Stimulant medications should be avoided in patients with congenital structural heart diseases due to possible risk of sudden unexplained death.

questions.question_text: Which autoimmune disorder is associated with OCD in children?
questions.explanation: . Some children appear to develop obsessive -compulsive symptoms associated with beta haemolytic streptococcal infection and this presentation represents a minority of OCD cases in this population.

questions.question_text: Sibling rivalry disorders usually emerge in which of the following time periods?

options.text: Within a year after the birth of the sibling
Within 1 month after the birth of the sibling
Within 6 months after the birth of the sibling
Within 4 months after the birth of the sibling
Within 3 months after the birth of the sibling

correct_answer.text: Within 6 months after the birth of the sibling

correct_answers.text: Within 6 months after the birth of the sibling

questions.explanation: . Sibling rivalry disorder is characterised by a child having an abnormally intense negative feelings toward an immediately younger sibling.

questions.question_text: In child psychiatry, shaping refers to

options.text: Reinforcing positive behaviour; ignoring negative behaviour
Punishing negative behaviour; praising positive behaviour
Neither reinforcing nor punishing observed behaviours
Differential reinforcement of behaviours other than the desired outcome
Gradual reinforcement of behaviours approximating desired outcome

correct_answer.text: Gradual reinforcement of behaviours approximating desired outcome

correct_answers.text: Gradual reinforcement of behaviours approximating desired outcome

questions.explanation: . Shaping was introduced by Skinner, initially with training of pigeons.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has the best evidence for use in childhood depression?
questions.explanation: . Several studies have demonstrated efficacy with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRI) antidepressants, especially using fluoxetine. Fluoxetine is the best-studied antidepressant with the strongest efficacy data.

questions.question_text: Most children with selective mutism also meet diagnostic criteria for which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: . Selective mutism is a disorder characterized by a persistent failure to speak in specific settings (school) despite the full use of language at home or with family.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about Rett's syndrome is true?

options.text: Characterised by progressive lack of acquired abilities
There is apparent lack of normal development in the first 2 years of life
Is associated with microcephaly at birth

correct_answer.text: Characterised by progressive lack of acquired abilities

correct_answers.text: Characterised by progressive lack of acquired abilities

questions.explanation: . Rett syndrome is a neurodevelopmenal disorder that affects girls almost exclusively.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is characterised by impaired ability to recognise words, slow and inaccurate reading and poor comprehension?
questions.explanation: . Reading disorders are present in approximately 75 percent of children and adolescents with learning disorders.

questions.question_text: Reactive attachment disorder is generally diagnosed before the age of
questions.explanation: . RAD is diagnosed before 5 yrs, and may manifest as either inhibited or disinhibited subtypes.

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric co-morbidity associated with Asperger's syndrome is
questions.explanation: . Psychiatric co morbidity is high with depression being the most common.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a good prognostic factor in children with conduct disorder?

options.text: Having a family member convicted for violent conduct

questions.explanation: . Protective factors conferring a better prognosis include 1. Female gender 2. High IQ 3. Resilient temperament 4. Good parenting among several others.

questions.question_text: Regarding the aetiology of ADHD, all of the following are true except

options.text: There is a 50% increased risk in monozygotic twins
Siblings of hyperactive children have about twice the increased risk of having the disorder
Neuroimaging shows lower cerebral blood flow and metabolic rates in the frontal lobe areas of children with ADHD than in controls
Predominant serotonin dysregulation is seen in the prefrontal cortex

correct_answer.text: Predominant serotonin dysregulation is seen in the prefrontal cortex

correct_answers.text: Predominant serotonin dysregulation is seen in the prefrontal cortex

questions.explanation: . Predominant involvement of neurotransmitters DA and NA dysregulation is seen in the prefrontal cortex.

questions.question_text: Which of the following suggests a diagnosis of bulimia rather than anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: . Poor impulse control is suggestive more of a diagnosis of bulimia than anorexia.

questions.question_text: Pica typically occurs during
questions.explanation: . Pica is characterised by persistent eating of non-nutritive substances at a developmentally inappropriate age and it lasts for more than a month.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-old girl presents with some uncoordinated movements of her limbs. She had a history of fever and sore throat six months ago. Which is the most likely cause for her presentation?
questions.explanation: . Pharyngeal infection with Lancefield Group A Beta Hemolytic streptococci triggers rheumatic fever 2-4 weeks later, in the susceptible 2% of the population.

questions.question_text: What treatment is not preferred for a child with a hyperkinetic disorder?
Which drug is now specifically contraindicated in children and adolescents due to increased risk of suicide?
questions.explanation: . Paroxetine is not approved for the treatment of patients younger than 18 years of age.

questions.question_text: The most common cause of co-morbidity in children and adolescents with bipolar disorder is
questions.explanation: . Overlap of many symptoms seen in pediatric BD and those of ADHD make it even more difficult to diagnose BD.

questions.question_text: Manifestations of the oppositional defiant disorder are almost invariably present

options.text: In the presence of other adults

questions.explanation: . Oppositional defiant disorder (ODD) is characterised by an enduring pattern of negative, hostile, and defiant behaviour, without serious violations of societal norms or the rights of others.

questions.question_text: The most common co-morbid disorders seen in Tourette's syndrome is
questions.explanation: . OCD and ADHD are commonly comorbid with tics.; depression, anxiety, impulse and conduct disorders and other behavioural problems.

questions.question_text: The most common co-morbidity in patients with Tourette's syndrome is;
questions.explanation: . Obsessive -compulsive symptoms or disorder (OCD) has been found to co-exist in 1/3rd to 2/3rds of children and adolescents with Tourette's disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is found to be effective in treating adolescent inhalant abuse?
questions.explanation: . No proven therapy is available for inhalant users.

questions.question_text: Which of the following should be used as a first choice treatment in children and adolescents with acute manic or mixed episodes?
questions.explanation: . NICE guidelines on bipolar disorder in children and adolescents suggest using adult medication guidelines but in lower doses.

questions.question_text: Which neurotransmitter system is commonly postulated to be involved in the aetiology of Tourettes syndrome?
questions.explanation: . Neurotransmitter abnormalities thought to underlie tic disorder such as Tourette's include a functional excess of dopamine system as antipsychotics reduce symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following has confirmed the most evidence for successful treatment of OCD compared to any of the other anxiety disorders of childhood?

options.text: Combination of both medication and CBT

correct_answer.text: Combination of both medication and CBT

correct_answers.text: Combination of both medication and CBT

questions.explanation: . Most treatment guidelines for children and adolescents with mild to moderate OCD recommend a trial of cognitive-behavioural therapy prior to initiating medication.

questions.question_text: The total sleeping time of a newborn baby is approximately
questions.explanation: . Most newborns sleep for 16 to 17 hours in total each day and will sleep up to 6 hours at a time.

questions.question_text: Which is the first line drug in an 8-year-old with uncomplicated ADHD?
questions.explanation: . Methylphenidate, an indirect sympathomimetic that increases release of DA and NA is usually the first line treatment and is generally well tolerated in ADHD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following may be a long-term effect of prescribing high doses of methylphenidate over long periods without drug holidays?
questions.explanation: . Methylphenidate can cause loss of appetite and weight loss, insomnia, headaches, nausea and vomiting, anxiety, dysphoria, rarely tics and raised BP. At higher doses, psychosis and seizures have been reported. Growth suppression may be a long-term outcome of high doses over long periods without drug holidays.

questions.question_text: The commonest age of presentation for school refusal is
questions.explanation: . Mean onset of separation anxiety disorder is at age 7.5 years. Mean onset of school refusal is at age 10.3 years.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is reported more commonly in females?
questions.explanation: . Mathematics disorder alone is estimated to occur in about 1 percent of school -age children, that is, approximately 1 of every 5 children with learning disorder.

questions.question_text: All of the following are risk factors for adolescent suicide except
questions.explanation: . Males commit more suicide at adolescence than females.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a biological risk factor associated with conduct disorder?
questions.explanation: . Low CSF serotonin is associated with impulsivity and aggressive responses. In some cases full blown conduct disorder may be the effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptom is least commonly reported in children with bipolar disorder?
questions.explanation: . Irritability, or having low threshold for experiencing distress in response to common triggers, is a very sensitive, but not at all specific characteristic of BD; almost all children with BD exhibit some form of irritability.

questions.question_text: Developmentally inappropriate social relatedness seen before the age of 5 following prolonged separation from caregivers is called
questions.explanation: . Indiscriminate sociability following prolonged separation from caregivers is seen in reactive attachment disorder - disinhibited type.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of ADHD among girls between the ages of 5 -15 according to DSM -4 criteria is
questions.explanation: . In the USA, ADHD is estimated at 3 -5%, which is based on DSM criteria. There is a male predominance of 3:1.

questions.question_text: The overall prevalence of psychiatric disorders in adolescence is;
questions.explanation: . In the UK, 16 -20% adolescents have a 'diagnosable' psychiatric condition.

questions.question_text: What proportion of adolescents admits to having had suicidal ideas in the UK in the past year?
questions.explanation: . In the UK an estimated 15% of adolescents admit to suicidal ideation in the past year.

questions.question_text: The percentage of reading difficulties in children in Britain is estimated to be around
questions.explanation: . In the UK (and in most of the English-speaking developed world) it is generally recognized that between 4 to 7% of children have specific reading disorder - developmental dyslexia - at any given time.

questions.question_text: Tom is a 7-year-old boy who was diagnosed with ADHD recently. His mum wants to know about the long term prognosis of symptoms. Which of the following symptoms is most likely to remit first?
questions.explanation: . In the natural course of ADHD, hyperactivity is usually the first symptom to remit and distractibility is the last.

questions.question_text: According to the Isle of Wight survey, the commonest psychiatric disorder in childhood is
questions.explanation: . In the Isle of White study, CD was found to be the most common psychiatric disorder amongst 10 -11 year olds.

questions.question_text: The Cambridge study by Farrington et al. identified risk factors in children between 8 -10 years that can predict later delinquent behaviour by the age of 32. Which one among the following is not a risk factor identified by this study?
questions.explanation: . In the Cambridge Study in Delinquent Development, 411 South London males have been followed up from age 8 to age 32.
